extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural community (applicants, awardees, institutional administrators, and peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational guidance for NIH extramural applicants, reviewers, and grant recipients describing what systems and processes remain available and what actions should be taken (or delayed) during a lapse in federal appropriations. Covers submissions, peer review, awards, reporting, payments, and animal/human-safety contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA systems availability and support
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Systems will be operational, but with limited support. Use is restricted to excepted activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA will provide limited end-user support for excepted/approved staff and excepted programs. The eRA service desk will not be operational. If applicants encounter system issues when applying, they should submit an eRA service desk ticket to document the issue. NIH will take this into consideration for accepting late applications when operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail, phone, fax, and postal mail contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: For the duration of the funding lapse, NIH extramural employees will be prohibited from working (remotely or in the office), and there will be no access to voice mail, e-mail, fax, or postal mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail requiring someone to sign/accept may not be received. All other postal mail, fax, and voice mail communications will not be acted upon until after operations resume. It is recommended that you delay sending such communications until after operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central e-mail boxes for policy and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All central e-mail boxes and web ticketing systems for questions related to NIH grants policy and compliance will not be operational during the funding lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect policy or compliance questions submitted to central mailboxes/ticketing systems to be answered until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human participant safety emergency contact
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of an emergency involving human participant safety in NIH-funded research, contact Dr. Jon Lorsch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the named contact as the route for urgent human-safety issues since normal NIH contact channels are unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of grant applications — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should continue to submit applications in accordance with the due dates outlined in the Notices of Funding Opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be accepted and reviewed once operations resume. Continue to meet posted due dates; NIH will not process submissions until operations resume but will accept them into systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov electronic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov will be open and can accept electronic applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Grants.gov will accept submissions, applications will not be processed by NIH until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASSIST multi-project application submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ASSIST system will remain available and can accept multi-project applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications submitted through ASSIST will not be processed by NIH until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting system issues for late-submission consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicants encounter system issues when applying, they should submit an eRA service desk ticket to document the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting issues via service desk ticket may be considered by NIH for accepting late applications when operations resume, acknowledging that service desk support itself is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial peer review meetings suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: During the funding lapse, the NIH will not be able to conduct initial peer review meetings—whether in-person or through teleconferences or other electronic media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH staff will not be able to send or receive email messages or update website information. When operations resume, meetings will be re-scheduled and pending applications processed as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of peer review results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results (including final impact scores and summary statements) of some peer review meetings that took place prior to the shutdown may not be available until operations resume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should monitor national news for resumption of government operations and then check NIH website for updates; results will be released as soon as possible after resumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access to Internet Assisted Review (IAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who had agreed to serve on NIH review panels scheduled during the lapse will have access to the IAR site and can upload initial critiques and scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support will not be available. Reviewers scheduled to travel will not be able to board and will be sent instructions about reservations; reviewers should await NIH communication after operations resume for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council review suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH will not be able to conduct Advisory Council review meetings during the funding lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No applications will be processed for Council review or taken to Council meetings during that time. Meetings will be re-scheduled when operations resume; the NIH Executive Secretary will contact Council members with detailed information as soon as possible after resumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currently active grant awards — permitted activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For the duration of the funding lapse, all work and activities performed under currently active NIH grant awards may continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some reporting and administrative functions may be limited; see related entries on RPPRs, NoAs, NCEs, and prior approvals for constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPR) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For any annual or final RPPRs due during the funding lapse, eRA Commons will be available and users must submit reports on time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH staff will review reports after operations resume; timely submission remain required despite limited staff availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Award (NoAs) processing
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of excepted programs, no NIH grant awards will be processed for the duration of the funding lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards processed before the lapse that have an issue date during the lapse will not be sent to recipients until operations resume. This delay does not affect the start date or issue date of awards, only when the award document is sent and available in eRA Commons. In the absence of receiving the NoA, institutions may use pre-award costs authority at their own risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cost extension (NCE) notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons will remain accessible; recipients should submit NCE notifications in accordance with standard requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff will not be available to review and approve requests. Requests for second or greater NCEs, which require prior approval, may be submitted but will not be reviewed until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: General access to eRA Commons and OER-supported systems
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons will be accessible during the funding lapse for viewing submitted applications and processing certain actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can access Commons to view applications, access IAR, process Commons Registration, xTrain documents, Closeout documents, and FCOI notifications, but limited staff support will be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval requests and other communications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH extramural employees will have no access to voice mail or e-mail during the funding lapse; prior approval requests and other communications will not be received until operations resume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended to delay sending such communications until after operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to HHS PSC/Payment Management System (PMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards received prior to the lapse, recipients may continue drawing funds during an appropriations lapse; PMS will remain operational to continue processing drawdown requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing internal controls will continue. Recipients of awards with restrictive terms and conditions, or requests that trigger PMS edit checks and/or drawdown limit controls, may not be able to draw down funds. Recipients can continue to complete and submit Federal Financial Reports (FFR) in PMS, but NIH staff will not review/process FFRs until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal welfare / OLAW business processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare (OLAW) business processes are funded by annual appropriations and are not designated as excepted activities; no activities associated with the OLAW mission will continue during the funding lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHS-funded institutions are encouraged to delay sending Assurance documents, preliminary or final reports of noncompliance, or IACUC suspensions until after operations resume. OLAW will extend deadlines for reporting activities as necessary. Institutions remain responsible for ongoing local support and oversight to ensure animal welfare and compliance with PHS Policy during the lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiries and points of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct inquiries regarding these policies to the Office of Policy for Extramural Research Administration (OPERA), Office of Extramural Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed OPERA contact email for questions; anticipate delays in responses until operations resume.
